This reads like "please add transparency on quest" but like 20 times longer because an LLM has been asked to write an essay about it. 

The most amusing tell is the mention of Quest 1, struggling under [recent](https://ask.vrchat.com/t/developer-update-4-may-2023/17924) [updates ](https://www.uploadvr.com/vrchat-quest-1-support-end-date/) indeed. 

VRChat works fine on Quest 3, I don't think there is really a surplus of performance so spend on anything.

details:
Suggestion:

Currently, VRChat does not allow PhysBones on materials with transparency. While this prevents potential performance issues, it also forces creators to use extra polygons instead of simple transparent textures for small details like eyebrows, eyelashes, hair strands, or ribbons. This results in higher poly counts and unnecessary performance strain, especially on standalone devices.

Proposed Solution

1. Allow PhysBones on Transparent Materials (For Small Objects Only)

Enable PhysBones for small transparent objects (e.g., eyebrows, eyelashes, hair strands, ribbons).

Restrict this option for large transparent objects to avoid performance abuse.

2. Add a User-Controlled Visibility Setting for Transparent PhysBone Materials

All Players: Everyone sees the transparency.

Friends Only: Only friends see it, reducing strain in public lobbies.

Just You: Only the user sees their own transparency, avoiding performance impact for others.

Off: Disables transparent PhysBones entirely for maximum performance.

3. Quest-Specific Optimization

The Quest 3 has significantly more GPU and CPU power compared to the Quest 2. It can handle transparent PhysBones by default, so this option should be enabled by default on Quest 3 while remaining off on Quest 2 and older headsets unless manually turned on.

On Quest 2 and older devices, the option could be off by default to maintain performance, but users should still have the ability to turn it on for personal use.

The Quest 1 could have this feature disabled entirely, as it is already struggling with VRChat’s recent updates.

Why This Change Matters

Lower Polygon Counts: Creators can use transparent textures instead of extra geometry.

Better Performance: Less complex meshes mean fewer physics calculations.

More User Control: Players can adjust transparency settings based on their hardware and preference.

Quest 3 Optimizations: The Quest 3 has more processing power and can fully support this feature without significant performance loss.
title: Feature Request – Allow Small Transparent PhysBone Materials with Selective Visibility Options
